title: The academy Build tutorials still teach a replay-unsafe reducer pattern, generating IDs inside the reducer via generateId()
content:
This records a **documentation bug**, not stack behaviour. Several `03-Build` tutorial pages instruct the reader to generate IDs inside the reducer, and one of them explicitly blesses it as the recommended approach:

- `03-Build/02-DocumentModelCreation/05-ImplementDocumentReducers.md:118` — *"Notice that `addTodoItemOperation` uses `generateId()` from `document-model/core` to create a unique ID. This is the recommended pattern — the ID is generated in the reducer, not passed from the UI."* Reducer-side `const id = generateId();` appears at lines 92, 136, 205, 254, 288 and 314.
- `03-Build/02-DocumentModelCreation/03-SpecifyDocumentOperations.md:46, 51, 150, 206` — teaches omitting `id` from the operation input because "the reducer will generate it automatically".
- `03-Build/01-ManualTodoTutorial/03-ImplementOperationReducers.md:107, 122` — same reducer body, with "We generate a unique ID using `generateId()`" in the walkthrough.
- Also `02-SpecifyTheStateSchema.md:39` and `07-ExampleToDoListRepository.md:22`.

`generateId` is non-deterministic. In `packages/shared/document-model/utils.ts` it is:

```typescript
export function generateId(method?: "UUIDv4"): string {
  if (method && method.toString() !== "UUIDv4") { throw new Error(...); }
  return globalThis.crypto.randomUUID();
}
```

Calling it in a reducer means two peers folding the same operation log produce different IDs, and a document replayed from its own log no longer reproduces its stored state — the same class of failure as the `initialState` hash mismatch.

**The rest of the docs are right.** `02-Learn/08-deep-dives/01-reducers-in-depth.mdx:13` states "No time or randomness. No `Date.now()`, no `Math.random()`, no `crypto.randomUUID()` — those values come from action inputs." `02-Learn/03-document-models/03-actions-and-reducers.mdx` shows `generateId()` called **in the editor before dispatch** and includes a quiz answer explaining that random fallbacks make a reducer non-deterministic. The purity rule and the Learn track are correct; the Build tutorial pages are stale legacy.

A corroborating staleness signal on the same pages: the Manual Todo walkthrough still says "Powerhouse uses Immer.js" where the stack uses Mutative.

Correct pattern: put `id: OID!` in the operation input schema, call `generateId()` in the editor, and use `action.input.id` in the reducer.

Provenance: file/line audit of academy `03-Build/**` versus `02-Learn/**` at academy 6.2.2-dev.45, with the `generateId` implementation read from `packages/shared/document-model/utils.ts:4-12`.
description: generateId() returns crypto.randomUUID(), so reducer-side ID generation breaks replay determinism. The Learn track and the purity rule are correct; these legacy Build pages are stale.
